column1: # Deferred (2026-11-18): CUTOFF review for wide hits. BB0026 (55 kb), BB0018 (55), BB0017 (30), BB0009/BB0041 (25), BB0097 (20).
# A wide hit is usually a symptom, not a cause: antiSMASH reports first-to-last contributing gene, so one
# distant wrongly-credited gene stretches the span and the genes between it and the real locus come along
# passively. BB0026's rubradirin hit was 95.9 kb with 35 CDS: 8 reference genes, 5 wrongly credited, 22 passive.
# Re-measure the spans after the manual not-terms are in; only lower CUTOFF if hits are still wide once the
# spurious credits are gone. Correlation of span with extra genes (r=0.87) reflects the shared cause, not CUTOFF driving it.
# Fixed (2026-11-18): BB0007 lost its own BGC0001072 (simocyclinone) to an automatic `not Condensation`.
# simD6 is a Cglyc-A-PCP didomain, so Condensation is carried by 1 of the 5 reference A-domain genes --
# present, but below the signature threshold, so module_exclusions() did not see it and excluded it anyway.
# module_exclusions() now tests every domain a group's genes carry (observed_domains), not just signatures.
# An audit of all 59 rules found this was the only term whose exclusion broke a reference subcluster, and
# dropping it changes no hit among the 358 BGCs that formed protoclusters. Rerun antiSMASH to confirm recovery.
# BB0094 (2,3-diaminopropionic acid) -- weakest rule in the set, keep but tighten when possible.
# One reference subcluster only (capreomycin: cmnB PALP, cmnK OCD_Mu_crystall), so two broad Pfam
# families with no comparative evidence to narrow them and no reference-gene property to exclude on.
# rapamycin (BGC0001040) fires because rapL, the lysine cyclodeaminase making pipecolate, is an
# OCD_Mu_crystall member -- a genuine family-level collision, not a fixable annotation error.
# NOT covered by antiSMASH's aminopolycarboxylic-acid rule: that fires on AesA+AesB+AesC and shares
# no model with this one. Both merely hit the same EDHA loci (BGC0001587, BGC0002568). Dropping BB0094
# would lose capreomycin/friulimicin/zwittermicin/sulfazecin with nothing replacing it.
# Needs: a specific 2,3-Dap aminotransferase (SbnA/cmnB-like) model to replace PALP.
# CUTOFF re-measured (2026-11-18) after the manual not-terms, on the current MIBiG 4.0 run.
# BB0026 / BGC0000141 is still 95.9 kb / 35 CDS / 28 passive, but that span is INTRINSIC to the
# reference subcluster, not an artifact: in data/genbanks/BB0026_D-rubranitrose/SC0041.gbk the eight
# genes sit in three blocks -- rubN2 at 1 kb, rubN4/N5/N8 at 38-42 kb, rubN1/N3/N6/N7 at 91-96 kb.
# CUTOFF 55 is what it takes to link them, so lowering it would split a genuine subcluster. Do not.
# BB0051 37.1 (45, median 7.5 -- one outlier only). Check each against its reference gene layout the
# same way before changing a CUTOFF: a wide reference subcluster needs a wide CUTOFF.
# Wrong gene reported for a cds() term -- an antiSMASH BUG, not a rule or model problem.
# BB0026 / BGC0000141 reports Epimerase against rubP3 (53.8 kb) and leaves the correct gene rubN6
# (93.2 kb) passive; BB0017 / BGC0000654 likewise reports plaU instead of plaA7. A sweep of every
# rule against its own reference BGCs found exactly these two cases, both on Epimerase.
# Cause: CDSCondition.is_satisfied (common/hmm_rule_parser/rule_parser.py) ORs the per-gene results
# into a bare boolean and returns ConditionMet(xor(results, negated)) with no matches and no
# ancillary_hits, so a cds() term never reports WHICH gene satisfied it. The rubP3 credit instead
# comes from the rubN2 anchor: apply_cluster_rules anchors on every CDS with a hit in turn and
# measures CUTOFF from the anchor, and rubN2 (pos 1140) reaches rubP3 at 51.7 kb but not rubN6 at
# 91.1 kb. Detection is correct either way -- only the reported gene list is wrong.
# A pull request for this is already open (user, 2026-11-18); no action needed here.
# This is why the epimerase model below is NOT needed to fix these two gene lists -- the PR fixes
# them. The model is still wanted for the genuinely ambiguous clusters, where Epimerase matches 7-8
# genes in one cluster (BGC0002085, BGC0002088) and no reference-gene property separates them.
# SUPERIORS (2026-11-18, revised 2026-11-19 after checking each pair biologically, not just by gene set).
# KEPT -- the superior is a genuine tailoring of the inferior's product, so where the extra gene is
# present the derivative really is what the cluster makes:
#   BB0091<BB0020  hydroxymalonyl-ACP is the on-pathway precursor; Methyltransf_3 (fkbG/asm17) O-methylates
#                  it to methoxymalonyl-ACP. 20 hits dropped, all ansamycins/macrolides. 15 kept.
#   BB0084<BB0098  CCR+HBDH pair vs the same operon plus the KSIII sitting between them (divRST); verified
#                  in all 7 overlaps. 7 dropped, 17 kept.
#   BB0128<BB0041  C-1027's benzoxazolinate IS methoxylated (SMILES starts COC1=CC2=C(NC(=O)...O2); sgcD4
#                  is the O-MT), and the chromophore has only one such moiety. 3 dropped, 3 kept.
#   BB0055<BB0121  MppO hydroxylates FREE L-enduracididine made by MppP/MppQ/MppR, and the mppO knockout
#                  gives dideoxy-mannopeptimycins, so both residues are normally betahEnd (PMID 16298295).
#                  Enduracididine is a transient intermediate there. 1 dropped, 1 kept (enduracidin).
#   BB0124<BB0097  beta-tyrosine is the precursor of C-1027's chlorinated dihydroxy-beta-Phe. 2 dropped;
#                  BB0124 keeps maduropeptin (its other reference) and 4 more hits.
# REMOVED -- BB0089<BB0016 was NOT biologically sound. Platensimycin/platencin make ent-kauranol and
#   ent-atiserene (PtmT3 / PtmT1), chemically distinct from the brasilicardin/KS-505a tricyclic
#   diterpenoids; the two rules share only the upstream GGPP -> ent-CPP steps. These are parallel diterpene
#   pathways, not precursor/derivative, and the SUPERIORS would have deleted BB0089 on its own reference
#   BGC0001140 (platensimycin/platencin), leaving it with zero hits. Both rules should stand.
# Net: 33 redundant hits removed (523 -> 490).
# Checked and deliberately NOT paired: BB0025/BB0023 and BB0059/BB0105, where the inferior credits genes
# the superior misses -- co-occurring building blocks in one cluster, not a subset relationship.
# Lesson: a strict-superset gene relationship is necessary but NOT sufficient. Before adding SUPERIORS,
# check whether the superior's extra gene really tailors the inferior's product, and check whether the
# inferior would lose a hit on one of its OWN reference BGCs (4 of the 6 pairs did; only BB0089's was wrong).
